source.note: Milestone one. No video, no reconstruction. Every dimension comes from a catalog template, so the scene is metric by construction and needs no scale reference. A video-derived scene DOES need one -- see marker_config below.
source.frame_convention: Robot base at the origin. Bench top surface at z=0, so the arm mounts flush to it. Bench extends in +y, in front of the robot.
source.composition_rationale: Chosen for collider coverage rather than object variety: box (static + dynamic) and sdf (normal, small-feature, and extreme-aspect-ratio). convex_decomposition is deliberately NOT covered here -- see known_gaps.

objects.note: Static fixture. Sunk by its own 0.04 m thickness so its top surface lands exactly at z=0, the robot base plane. MATTERIX names sim/real table size mismatch as a direct cause of a real-world failure, so this is the first dimension to measure on the real bench.
Dynamic box. Carries plate_center at (0, -0.045, 0.105), a keypoint that is NOT at the prim origin -- which is the case that catches an emitter writing keypoints relative to the wrong frame.
SDF collider, 70 x 95 mm. The only vessel in the catalog whose dimensions survived review unchanged.

SDF with small features: a 1 mm wall and a 14 mm cavity stress SDF resolution. Also free-standing at a 6.25:1 aspect ratio, so it tips past 9 degrees of lean -- expect this to be the object that moves first if the T3 settle test ever fails.
SDF at an extreme aspect ratio: 100 mm wide by 15 mm tall, with a 1.2 mm wall. A uniform-resolution SDF that is fine for the beaker can under-resolve this lid-less dish entirely.
